Stock $3.72 (13 October) to about $1.57 (6 November); co-founder sold 7.66mn shares 3-5 November and is pushing for a sale; two directors won a majority of votes cast but not of shares outstanding on 30 October and hold over.
checks: Built before results. Date from company release (12 October). 2Q26 figures, debt by facility, CIP, Phase 0-1 need, Texas Tech NTP from 10-Q and release on EDGAR, confirmed by a fresh subagent. Convert, MUFG amendment ($25mn fee, waiver, about $56mn amortization avoided) and TensorWave terms from 8-Ks and fact sheet, confirmed; 9 August signing date per 10-Q; lapse per 3 November release. Wording corrected on substantial doubt (alleviated by management plans) and director vote. Price $1.57 on 6 November confirmed (StockAnalysis). Not checked: consensus, broker targets, short interest (single source), insider sales. AMD support size undisclosed. Consensus thin and stale: Provisional.
consensus_thesis: Brokers still rate Fermi a Buy as an option on scarce Texas power assets (about 1.5 GW of landed turbines, 6 GW of air permits, a signed 15-year TensorWave lease with AMD credit support), but at about $1.57 on 6 November, down from $3.72 on 13 October, with about 20% of float short (single source), substantial-doubt language in the 10-Q (which management says its plans alleviate) and the co-founder selling and pushing for a sale, the tape prices distress or heavy dilution.
headline: 3Q26 is a funding and survival test, not an earnings event: the $6.5bn TensorWave lease lapsed unclosed on 31 October for want of project financing, cash was $92mn at 30 June against about $2bn needed in 12 months, and the market cap (about $1.0bn) sits below book PP&E.
kona: Fermi is the cautionary case for gas-powered, behind-the-meter AI campuses: a signed lease with a big-name credit backstop still did not close because construction financing was a condition precedent, while turbine warehouse loans at 12-14% ran up the clock. For Kona the lesson is to line up project debt (or a tenant prepayment) in parallel with the lease rather than after it, avoid lease closing conditions that hinge on its own financing, and keep equipment debt short of covenants tied to signing a lease by a fixed date.

questions.question: Project-level financing is a closing condition of the TensorWave lease, which lapsed on 31 October despite AMD credit support from 13 October. Which lenders have issued term sheets, for how much against the roughly $3bn Phase 0-1 need, and what new closing date has TensorWave agreed?
questions.why: Tests the pillar everything else depends on.

questions.question: The 10-Q cites about $2bn needed in 12 months. What was cash at 30 September after about $382mn net convert proceeds and the $25mn MUFG fee, how many months of runway is that, and will the substantial-doubt language be repeated?
questions.why: Sets dilution risk and the equity's value.

questions.question: The $77.3mn Keystone loan must be prepaid without an approved customer agreement by 31 December, and the $444.9mn MUFG loan at about 12% matures 10 August 2027. Is a waiver or refinancing agreed, and who joins the new MUFG syndicate?
questions.why: Near-dated secured debt sits ahead of the convert.

questions.question: Texas Tech requires notice to proceed by 31 December, conditioned on a 200 MW Phase 1 lease and financing. If TensorWave has not closed, what happens to the site rights, and has an extension been agreed?
questions.why: The land is the core asset in the bull floor.

questions.question: The 13 August release promised about 200 MW of commercial power within six months, but the call said first power of 210 MW on 1 July 2027. Which is right, is the Phase One EPC contract signed, and are the Hillcore definitive agreements (due about 9 November) done?
The co-founder claims indications of $10-20bn enterprise value were rebuffed. Is the board running a strategic review, and what is the status of the EDNY subpoena and SEC request?

sections.body: Developing Project Matador, a behind-the-meter gas-power and AI data center campus near Amarillo, Texas, on a 99-year Texas Tech ground lease, with an ambition of about 17 GW (gas turbines, a Hillcore-funded gas plant, grid, solar and later nuclear). Earns modified-net lease rent with 2.5% escalators, fuel passed through; TensorWave fact sheet guides about 75-80% project NOI margin. Pre-revenue; funded so far by the IPO, 12-17% equipment loans and a $431mn convert.
